raw_graphql_pull_request.body:
## Motivation

Fixes #46335.

SGLang cannot build a model from a compressed-tensors checkpoint that leaves a layer out of both `config_groups[*].targets` and `ignore`. llm-compressor writes such checkpoints for experts-only and attention-only quantization. It sets `"ignore": []` and stores every untargeted layer unquantized. SGLang raises on the first of those layers, before it loads any weight:

```
File ".../layers/quantization/compressed_tensors/utils.py", line 144, in find_matched_target
ValueError: Unable to find matching target for model.language_model.layers.0.linear_attn.in_proj_qkvz in the compressed-tensors config.
```

The checkpoint that hit this is [`bottlecapai/ThinkingCap-Qwen3.8-Flash-Next-NVFP4`](https://huggingface.co/bottlecapai/ThinkingCap-Qwen3.8-Flash-Next-NVFP4) at `df3922b2`. It is a `qwen4_exp` model whose config targets only the routed experts, with NVFP4 weight-only quantization:

```json
"config_groups": {"group_0": {"targets": ["re:.*mlp\\.experts\\.\\d+\\.(gate_proj|up_proj|down_proj)$"], "input_activations": null, "...": "..."}},
"ignore": [],
"sparsity_config": {}
```

A missing `packed_modules_mapping` is not the cause. Qwen4-Exp already maps `in_proj_qkvz` to `in_proj_qkv` and `in_proj_z`, and the config targets neither shard. Today the checkpoint only loads with `--json-model-override-args` replacing the whole `quantization_config`, with `"ignore": ["re:^(?!.*mlp\\.experts).*$"]` added.

vLLM has loaded untargeted layers as unquantized since vllm-project/vllm#41965. Its `find_matched_target` returns `None`, and the layer falls back to `UnquantizedLinearMethod`. This PR ports that change and logs the fallback once. It also keeps one check that vLLM dropped, described under Modifications.

Related work:

- #41836 and #41876 hit the same error on GLM-5.3-Flash and fix it for that model with a name mapper. Their tests expect `UnquantizedLinearMethod` for the affected projections, which is what this PR gives untargeted layers. That checkpoint is untested with this PR.
- #45898 adds `test_granitemoe_packed_modules.py`, which expects `Unable to find matching target` when the mapping is missing. With this PR that case no longer raises (see Compatibility).
- #38224 wraps `find_matched_target` in `try/except ValueError`. The wrapper becomes unnecessary.

## Modifications

```diff
 def find_matched_target(layer_name, module, targets, fused_mapping):
     match on layer name, then module class, then fused shards
-    if nothing matched: raise ValueError("Unable to find matching target ...")
+    if nothing matched: return None
+    if a fused layer matched only some shards: raise ValueError("Found different quantization schemes ...")

 def CompressedTensorsConfig.get_scheme_dict(layer, layer_name):
+    if no target matched: warning_once(...); return None
+    # get_quant_method then takes its existing unquantized paths

 def CompressedTensorsConfig.get_linear_scheme(layer, layer_name):
-    with suppress(ValueError):
-        sparsity_scheme = sparsity_scheme_map[find_matched_target(...)]
+    matched_target = find_matched_target(...)
+    if matched_target is not None:
+        sparsity_scheme = sparsity_scheme_map[matched_target]
```

- In `compressed_tensors/utils.py`, `find_matched_target` returns `Optional[str]` and no longer raises when nothing matches. `_match_fused_layer` still returns `None` when no shard matches. When only some shards match, it now raises, because one fused weight cannot hold a quantized shard next to a bf16 one. Without that check, this PR would turn today's construction error into a silent bf16 load. `should_ignore_layer` already raises the same error for inconsistent `ignore` shards. This check is the one deliberate difference from vLLM.
- In `compressed_tensors/compressed_tensors.py`, `get_scheme_dict` returns `None` for an untargeted layer and logs one `warning_once`. The message names no layer, because `warning_once` caches on its arguments and a per-layer message would print 921 lines for this checkpoint. The sparsity lookup checks for `None` instead of catching `ValueError`. This change is required, since with `sparsity_config: {}` every linear layer would otherwise reach `sparsity_scheme_map[None]` and raise `KeyError`.
- The `get_lm_head_scheme` docstring and a comment in `test_compressed_tensors_lm_head.py` justified the code with the unmatched-layer error. That error is gone, so both now point to the unquantized path.
- Five cases join `test_compressed_tensors_mixed_precision.py`, the existing file for target and `ignore` matching:
  - `test_untargeted_linear_loads_unquantized` gives the reported `in_proj_qkvz` an `UnquantizedLinearMethod`.
  - `test_untargeted_experts_load_unquantized` covers an attention-only config, where `get_moe_scheme` returns `None` for the experts.
  - `test_untargeted_layers_are_logged` checks that the fallback logs a warning.
  - `test_partly_targeted_fused_layer_raises` covers the check on partly matched fused layers.
  - `test_fused_layer_matches_when_every_shard_matches` guards the all-shards path of the rewritten `_match_fused_layer`. No other compressed-tensors unit test reaches it.

### Compatibility

- A layer that matched a target before resolves exactly as before. Only the no-match branch changed.
- Checkpoints that raised `Unable to find matching target` now load, with the untargeted layers unquantized.
- A layer that is quantized in the checkpoint but whose SGLang name matches no target, as with the missing mapping in #45898, no longer fails at construction. It gets unquantized parameters that do not match the stored tensors, and the outcome depends on the model's `load_weights`. The warning is the signal. A fused layer with only some shards targeted still raises.
- A fused layer whose shards only partly match a `sparsity_config` target now raises. The old sparsity lookup swallowed that error.
- Reverting this PR restores the old error. Nothing is persisted.

## Accuracy Tests

The unit tests run on CPU. On unmodified `main`, four of the five new cases fail with the original error, and the fused-layer guard passes:

```
ERROR test_untargeted_linear_loads_unquantized   ValueError: Unable to find matching target for ...in_proj_qkvz ...
ERROR test_untargeted_experts_load_unquantized   ValueError: Unable to find matching target for ...mlp.experts.0.gate_proj ...
ERROR test_untargeted_layers_are_logged          ValueError: Unable to find matching target for ...in_proj_qkvz ...
ERROR test_partly_targeted_fused_layer_raises    AssertionError: "different quantization schemes" does not match "Unable to find matching target ..."
Ran 10 tests  FAILED (errors=4)
```

With this PR:

```
python3 test/registered/unit/layers/quantization/test_compressed_tensors_mixed_precision.py      Ran 10 tests  OK
python3 test/registered/unit/layers/quantization/test_compressed_tensors_lm_head.py              Ran 9 tests   OK
python3 test/registered/unit/layers/quantization/test_compressed_tensors_fp4_schemes.py          Ran 16 tests  OK
python3 test/registered/unit/layers/quantization/test_compressed_tensors_kv_cache.py             Ran 4 tests   OK
python3 test/registered/unit/layers/quantization/test_compressed_tensors_wna16_moe_no_linear.py  Ran 8 tests   OK
diff-cover coverage.xml --compare-branch=upstream/main --fail-under=60                           100% (10 of 10 changed lines)
```

Without a GPU, `pytest test/registered/unit/layers/quantization/` fails the same 151 tests with and without this PR. They are device errors in other quantization methods, such as `No CUDA GPUs are available`. With this PR, the 5 new tests also pass.

The layer-to-method parity check runs every module in the checkpoint's `model.safetensors.index.json` through the patched config, folded into SGLang's fused linears and per-layer MoE. The checkpoint's own config and the `ignore` workaround pick the same method for every layer:

```
linear prefixes: 921, moe prefixes: 49
  linear   921  as-shipped=UnquantizedLinearMethod        workaround=UnquantizedLinearMethod
  moe       49  as-shipped=CompressedTensorsW4A16Nvfp4MoE  workaround=CompressedTensorsW4A16Nvfp4MoE
mismatches: 0
```

The serving smoke test ran on one NVIDIA GB10 (sm121, aarch64, 128 GB unified memory). The image is SGLang `3c560089` with two local patches, the Qwen4 loader fix from #38900 and DFlash2 CUDA graph capture, plus this diff applied with `patch`. `3c560089` is 528 commits behind this branch's base `773cb938`. Between the two, the compressed-tensors package only gains a `get_moe_runner_backend` passthrough and changes two schemes this checkpoint does not use.

The server loaded the checkpoint as published, without `--json-model-override-args`. The draft model path points at a local snapshot of `incoai/Qwen3.8-Flash-Next-DFlash2` at `a22a1744`.

```
python3 -m sglang.launch_server --model-path bottlecapai/ThinkingCap-Qwen3.8-Flash-Next-NVFP4 \
  --revision df3922b21fc28a8604cc9b31451495690d155194 --tp 1 \
  --mem-fraction-static 0.863 --context-length 262144 --max-total-tokens 786432 \
  --moe-runner-backend flashinfer_cutlass --fp4-gemm-backend flashinfer_cutlass \
  --kv-cache-dtype fp8_e4m3 --page-size 64 --chunked-prefill-size 4096 \
  --reasoning-parser qwen3 --tool-call-parser qwen3_coder \
  --speculative-algorithm DFLASH --speculative-draft-model-path <DFlash2 snapshot> \
  --speculative-draft-model-quantization unquant --speculative-num-draft-tokens 4 \
  --linear-attn-verify-backend triton --mamba-ssm-dtype bfloat16 \
  --max-running-requests 1 --cuda-graph-max-bs-decode 1 --max-mamba-cache-size 20 \
  --schedule-policy lpm --ple-offload-embedding --ple-offload-backend file --ple-offload-dir /tmp/ple
```

The new warning appears once in the server log, and the experts get the NVFP4 MoE scheme:

```
[18:33:37] Some layers match no compressed-tensors target and are not in `ignore`; loading them unquantized.
[18:33:37] Acceleration for non-quantized schemes is not supported by Compressed Tensors. Falling back to UnquantizedLinearMethod
[18:33:37] Using CompressedTensorsW4A16Nvfp4MoE
[18:42:56] Load weight end. elapsed=559.15 s, type=Qwen4ExpForConditionalGeneration, quant=compressed-tensors ...
[18:46:22] The server is fired up and ready to roll!
```

`/generate` returns a coherent completion:

```
$ curl -s http://127.0.0.1:8019/generate -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
    -d '{"text": "The capital of France is", "sampling_params": {"max_new_tokens": 32, "temperature": 0}}'
" Paris. The capital of Germany is Berlin. The capital of Italy is Rome. The capital of Spain is Madrid. The capital of Portugal is\n\n<think>\nThe"
finish_reason: length (32 tokens), e2e_latency 1.08 s
```

GSM8K with sgl-eval 0.1.3 and thinking off:

```
sgl-eval run gsm8k --base-url http://127.0.0.1:8019/v1 --num-examples 200 --num-threads 2 \
  --temperature 0.7 --top-p 0.8 --seed 0 --max-tokens 4096 --chat-template-kwarg enable_thinking=false

200 examples (single-shot)  |  1614.5s  |  44 tok/s  |  71K tokens
score = 97.50%   truncated_rate = 0.50%   error_rate = 0.00%   avg_thinking_tokens = 0.0
```

Temperature 0.7 and top_p 0.8 are Qwen's non-thinking recommendation, and top_k 20 comes from the checkpoint's `generation_config.json`. sgl-eval has no flag for Qwen's recommended presence penalty, so it stayed at 0. There is no baseline GSM8K run with the `ignore` workaround. The parity check above shows both configs pick the same method for every layer.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

Not applicable. The change only touches config parsing and scheme selection. The parity check shows every layer gets the same method as with the workaround, so the forward pass is unchanged.

## Checklist

- [x] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit).
- [x] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests).
- [x] Update documentation according to [Write documentations](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#write-documentations). No user-facing docs or flags change.
- [x] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results according to [Test the accuracy](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#test-the-accuracy) and [Benchmark the speed](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#benchmark-the-speed).
- [x] Follow the SGLang code style [guidance](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#code-style-guidance).

+def _single_group_config(group):

+class TestUntargetedLayers(CustomTestCase):
+    """A layer that no group targets and `ignore` does not list is stored unquantized;
+    scheme lookup must not raise "Unable to find matching target" for it."""
+
+    def test_untargeted_linear_loads_unquantized(self):
+        config = _single_group_config(NVFP4_GROUP)
+        method = config.get_quant_method(_linear(), IN_PROJ_QKVZ)
+
+        self.assertIsInstance(method, UnquantizedLinearMethod)
+
+    def test_untargeted_experts_load_unquantized(self):
+        config = _single_group_config(FP8_GROUP)
+        scheme = config.get_moe_scheme(torch.nn.Module(), layer_name=EXPERTS_LAYER)
+
+        self.assertIsNone(scheme)
+
+    def test_untargeted_layers_are_logged(self):
+        """warning_once is lru_cache-wrapped; clear it to stay order-independent."""
+        logging.Logger.warning_once.cache_clear()
+        self.addCleanup(logging.Logger.warning_once.cache_clear)
+
+        config = _single_group_config(NVFP4_GROUP)
+        with self.assertLogs(compressed_tensors.logger, level="WARNING") as captured:
+            config.get_quant_method(_linear(), IN_PROJ_QKVZ)
+
+        self.assertIn("match no compressed-tensors target", "\n".join(captured.output))
+
+    def test_fused_layer_matches_when_every_shard_matches(self):
+        matched = find_matched_target(

+            module=torch.nn.Module(),
+            targets=["re:.*in_proj_qkv$", "re:.*in_proj_z$"],
+            fused_mapping=PACKED_MODULES_MAPPING,
